Gray |work=TROPICOS |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |accessdate=2009-11-25}} | range_map = Caesalpinia mexicana range map 2.png | range_map_caption = Natural range }} '''''Erythrostemon mexicanus''''', formerly ''Caesalpinia mexicana'',{{cite POWO| title = Erythrostemon mexicanus (Rose) Gagnon & G.P.Lewis| id = 60473357-2| access-date = 10 November 2022}} is a species of plant in the genus ''[[Erythrostemon]]'', within the pea family, [[Fabaceae]]. Common names include '''Mexican Bird of Paradise,''' '''Mexican holdback''',{{cite web |url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=CAME |title=Caesalpinia mexicana A. Gray Mexican holdback |work=PLANTS Database |publisher=United States Department of Agriculture |access-date=2009-12-03}} '''Mexican caesalpinia''', and '''tabachín del monte'''.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r9qqlxIOKTwC |title=How to Grow Native Plants of Texas and the Southwest |first=Jill |last=Nokes |edition=2 |publisher=University of Texas Press |year=2001 |isbn=978-0-292-75573-4 |pages=151–152}} It is native to the extreme lower [[Rio Grande Valley (Texas)|Rio Grande Valley]] of [[Texas]]{{cite web |url=http://aggie-horticulture.tamu.edu/ornamentals/natives/caesalpiniamexicana.htm |title=Mexican Caesalpinia, Mexican Poinciana |work=Benny Simpson's Texas Native Trees |publisher=Texas A&M University |accessdate=2009-01-28}} and to parts of [[Mexico]]: in the northeast and further south along the [[Gulf Coast of Mexico|Gulf coast]] as well as the Pacific coast in [[Nayarit]], [[Jalisco]], [[Colima]], and a small portion of [[Sinaloa]].{{cite book|first=Elbert L.|last=Little Jr.|title=Atlas of United States Trees|volume=3 (Minor Western Hardwoods)|year=1976|publisher=US Government Printing Office|lccn=79-653298|oclc=4053799|entry-url=https://archive.org/details/atlasofunitedsta1314litt/page/n69/mode/2up|entry=Map 27, ''Caesalpinia mexicana''}} ==Description== Mexican holdback is a small [[evergreen]] [[tree]] or large [[shrub]], reaching a height of {{convert|3|-|4.6|m|ft|abbr=on}} and a spread of {{convert|1.8|-|3|m|ft|abbr=on}}. [[Leaf|Leaves]] are [[Pinnate|bipinnately]]-compound and dark green.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AyWkIsLDca8C |title=Trees and Shrubs for the Southwest: Woody Plants for Arid Gardens |first=Mary |last=Irish |publisher=Timber Press |year=2008 |isbn=978-0-88192-905-8 |pages=141–142}} Each leaf has five to nine pinnae {{convert|4|-|9|cm|in|abbr=on}} in length.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vF_1X65cDxYC |first=Alfred |last=Richardson |title=Plants of the Rio Grande Delta |publisher=University of Texas Press |year=1995 |isbn=978-0-292-77070-6 |pages=103–104}} Pinnae are composed of four to five [[leaflet (botany)|leaflets]] that are {{convert|1|-|2.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|0.7|-|1.3|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide. Yellow, slightly fragrant [[flower]]s are produced on {{convert|7.6|-|15.2|cm|in|adj=on|abbr=on}} terminal [[Raceme|spikes]] of 10 to 30. Blooming takes place from February to July, often continuing to October. The [[fruit]] is a [[Dehiscence (botany)|dehiscent]] tan or yellow [[Legume|seedpod]] {{convert|5.1|-|7.6|cm|in|abbr=on}} in length. ==Uses== Mexican holdback is cultivated as an [[Ornamental plant|ornamental]] because of its showy flowers, lush, fine-textured foliage, and [[drought tolerance]].{{cite web |url=http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/pdffiles/FP/FP08200.pdf |first=Edward F |last=Gilman |title=''Caesalpinia mexicana'' Mexican Caesalpinia |work=IFAS Extension |publisher=University of Florida |date=October 1999 |accessdate=2010-11-23}} ==Ecology== ''Erythrostemon mexicanus'' is the [[Host (biology)|host]] plant for the [[caterpillar]]s of the curve-winged metalmark (''[[Emesis emesia]]'').{{cite web |url=http://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species?l=1649 |title=Curve-winged Metalmark ''Emesis emesia'' (Hewitson, 1867) |publisher=Butterflies and Moths of North America |accessdate=2009-11-29 |archive-date=2009-05-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090505192539/http://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species?l=1649 |url-status=dead }} ==References== {{commons category}} {{Wikispecies}} {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{cite web |url=http://ag.arizona.edu/pima/gardening/aridplants/Caesalpinia_mexicana.html |title=''Caesalpinia mexicana'' Mexican bird of paradise |work=Arid Plant List |publisher=University of Arizona |date=2006-03-16 |accessdate= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091221035329/http://ag.arizona.edu/pima/gardening/aridplants/Caesalpinia_mexicana.html |archive-date=2009-12-21 |url-status=dead }} {{Taxonbar|from1=Q42672348|from2=Q5016950}} [[Category:Caesalpinieae]] [[Category:Plants described in 1862]] [[Category:Flora of the Rio Grande valleys]] [[Category:Trees of Northern America]] [[Category:Flora of the Sierra Madre Oriental]]
